claims.text: A ~20 nm amorphous Al2O3 coating deposited by ALD will significantly improve the corrosion resistance of solutionized CoCrFeNi-based HEA fasteners relative to uncoated fasteners.
A ~20 nm amorphous Al2O3 coating deposited by ALD will significantly improve the mechanical durability of solutionized CoCrFeNi-based HEA fasteners relative to uncoated fasteners.
A ~20 nm amorphous Al2O3 coating deposited by ALD will significantly improve the room-temperature creep resistance of solutionized CoCrFeNi-based HEA fasteners relative to uncoated fasteners.
Well-solutionized CoCrFeNi-based HEA fasteners have a homogeneous microstructure.
The exposed surfaces of the uncoated fasteners are susceptible to corrosion and mechanical degradation under service conditions.
ALD at 150–250°C can produce a conformal, dense, approximately 20 nm Al2O3 film on the HEA fastener surface.
Post-deposition annealing at approximately 300°C improves adhesion of the alumina film.
Post-deposition annealing at approximately 300°C induces beneficial compressive residual stress at the coated surface.
The specified treatment yields a continuous, amorphous, well-adhered alumina film.
The alumina coating acts as a physical barrier that prevents corrosive species from reaching the underlying HEA.
Coating-induced surface compressive stresses hinder dislocation nucleation and propagation.
Hindering dislocation nucleation and propagation enhances room-temperature creep resistance.
Hindering dislocation nucleation and propagation enhances overall mechanical durability.
The coated fasteners will show more than a 30% improvement in corrosion resistance, measured through reduced corrosion current density.
The coated fasteners will accumulate less creep strain under constant load at room temperature than uncoated controls.
The coated fasteners will exhibit enhanced mechanical durability relative to uncoated controls.
Accelerated tests and preliminary studies support the barrier and stress-inducing effects of ALD alumina coatings.
